item.title: A train experience based on guilts: A train experience based on guilts
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard template, but with an extra "Experiments" section beneath the description

Elevator Pitch: The train is built to exploit the guilts of the beings that enters the train. As such, the beings must be capable of thoughts and feelings. It's like a personal "hell loop" for subjects except you only get a chance in "relieving yourself of the guilt".

Central Narrative: It is the first in a series of human experiments conducted to determine and understand the nature of the human beings of Earth. The experiment(s) tests the ability to overcome guilt and/or let things go. Future SCPs (experiments) could be to test for other traits such as insecurities and selfishness.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Hopefully, the SCP will be followed by tales which introduces a group of mysterious beings and further expand on the diversity of the universes.

Additional Notes: I started on the drafts before realizing I had to green-light the idea and not the SCP document itself

item.title: An Exelent Dentist: An Exelent Dentist
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article,

Genre: Horror/Psychological/Humour

Elevator Pitch:
The story revolves around an Ontario police department detective who discovers a string of disappearances leading him to a supernatural encounter and eventually recruitment into the SCP.

The SCP appears as a normal Dentist, family man, well respected and successful.

Central Narrative:

The SCP in this article is both setting and a lead in to another story I have in mind. The central horror narrative will be within the debriefing log of the Detective character of the story. The SCP itself will be a combination of light and creepy.

The SCP is intended to be Benign with a twist in further tales but for this story will be the creation point of the Detectives Horror story.

+ show block
– hide block

The Detective is an single minded workaholic with a talent for pattern recognition. He has been very successful the last few years professionally but at a great cost to his personal life which is now nonexistent. His mental state is also fraying due to overwork and PTSD.

His story begins after a medically induced coma and short term amnestics is administered to temporarily block memories which are harmful to the detective.

The Detective is being debriefed by an SCP Psychologist. Over the course of the debrief the Detectives memories will be challenged and teased out as the Amnestics wear off allowing him to gradually confront the horror of the SCP's progeny erupting from a persons teeth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
First off. I have a reoccurring nightmare about my teeth crumbling and being forced to spit out the pieces. I have talked to many people who have a similar dream and the internet says it is a pretty common one. This scares the fuck out of me and I bet it does a lot of people. But that is the cheap scares part.

Ideally I want the debrief to play like a slow reveal of the psychological degradation of the detective as he confronts his emerging memories of the events. Leading up to the death of someone he knew and purposefully led to the dentist in an effort to catch the SCP abducting the victim.

Additional Notes:

It's been a few year since I put pen to paper and I am looking forward to seeing if this idea is any good. I got super excited so this is actually already in second draft on my side. Thank you in advance for any commentary.

The Snow is Deep


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
How does the computer communicate from the center of the earth? I honestly can't imagine just handwaving this sorta thing… how does a signal travel from an incorporeal electronic device to physical electronic devices, through miles and miles of solid mass?

It's a Foundation long-distance communicator utilizing anomalous tech. Given that the Foundation has communication methods that can communicate extra-dimensionally and that most types of communication are intangible anyway, I don't feel communicating with an intangible computer is much of a stretch. And Foundation technology pretty much renders distance and matter separations irrelevant.

Why are there so many bodies down there? Like what is happening to make this occur? I can't imagine people are being turned incorporeal this often… If they are, why isn't that the SCP and not the bodies at the center of the earth?

The anomaly is the collection of everyone who has ever become intangible and fallen through the floor and it has been building up over many thousands of years. The bodies come from as far-flung sources as ancient trickster gods, experimental para-technology from an Occult war and quite a few from previous iterations of SCP-2000. Lastly while most bodies are dead, none have decomposed due to their intangible nature. As for some central object or entity causing this, that's simply not the case. This isn't a sinister plot or experiment gone wrong, this is an inevitability in a world with intangibility.

+ show block
– hide block

If the agents are deaf, dumb and blind (I don't know why because the post doesn't say, but I assume because of their status deep in the earth)… how can they tell the Foundation anything? They have no sensation (because tactile is out, due to their incorporeality).

I still think there isn't much to this narrative. It feels like a description of people suffering… but what is the arc here? Just "we're intangible, and at the center of the earth!" and then dying? (Also how would the agents even know about that they're in the center of the earth?)

Good point. I have changed the original post to explain how the agents understand and can interact with their situation.

Which is that they don't.

To the agents, they have been plunged into complete darkness, unable to move or touch anything, with a faint sensation of things (the other intangible people) filling the same space as them. To the agent with the computer, the computer is an outlet through by which they can call for help and via which may one day be rescued. So they desperately type at the computer, relying solely on muscle memory, not knowing whether what they are typing is being revived and unable to know if anyone has replied. The narrative is the story of that agents' experience, how they go from fearing, to hopeful, to desperate, and the implication that many other people have gone through that experience without the chance of salvation and will continue doing so indefinitely. It's a description of people suffering, but the story of one of those people shows how hopeless, prolonged and empty that suffering is.

item.title: SCP- Assimilator: SCP- Assimilator
item.content:encoded:
Item name: Assimilator

Greenlight: yes

Page layout: SCP article

Elevator pitch: A humanoid, resembling a male human, consisting of cells with anomalous biological characteristics, such as:

  • No presence of senescence.
  • Can modify their characteristics to provide enhanced regenerative abilities, and inhuman bursts of energy.
  • Immunity to all pathogens.

This SCP has been previously caught and studied, however it escaped Foundation custody and is now uncontained.

Central Narrative:
The cost of these properties is that the SCP needs more sustenance than a normal human. So, the entity finds it by eating food or hunting for live prey and/or carcasses to scavenge.

To hunt, it becomes a wraith-like mass consisting of mostly its cells to move like a swarm. Once in contact with prey, the mass encompasses it and begins stripping organic matter and nutrients from the organism, leaving only a husk. Once sated it returns to its normal form.

If the SCP gets severely injured, it will regenerate rapidly, however it will now need lots of energy replenishment, so it will consume large amounts of food or assimilate any living thing in its vicinity until sated.

The SCP can also shape shift into any creature by obtaining a sample of said creature’s DNA.

Hook/Attention:
The SCP creates backups for itself, in case it is destroyed, by infecting other creatures with its cells. The cells can also operate as a separate entity from the main body, which seeks out potential hosts.
Hosts fall into 3 categories:

"DORMANT": Cells lay low in the body, mimicking the host's cells to avoid an immune response and detection. Some become neurons to access the hosts memories and senses, and relays the information telepathically to the entity.

"ACTIVE": Upon the entity's order, cell replication rate increases and the cells take over the host, who is now under the control of the entity. The host is semi-sentient. This host will also mutate if severely damaged.

"REVIVAL": When sensing its destruction is imminent or when destroyed, the SCP’s cells in a particular host will begin replicating rapidly to replace the host with the entity. The reborn entity will retain all the memories of its previous body as well as the host's memories and skills.

The entity can also initiate rapid cellular degradation at will in itself to escape and revive in a host, or in an "ACTIVE" host to destroy it.

Hosts of SCP’s cells who are suffering from any disease or disorder, regardless of severity, will make a full recovery within 48 hours, assumed to be a by-product of the entity requiring a healthy host.

item.title: Want to earn Greenlighting Privileges and/or choose next month's front-page features?: Flight Signup Information
item.content:encoded:
I'm interested! How do I sign up to be a flight officer?

Simply create a New Post/post a new comment (don't use "reply") in this thread stating:

  • which Flight you are interested in (Flight 1, 2, or either)
  • a quick sentence about why you would like to be part of the mentoring process
  • optional: the name of the commander(s) you would like to work with, and one sentence why.

If a commander is interested in mentoring you, they will respond to your post.

I'm interested… but I think I want to work on my critique skills first/I didn't get picked this month. What can I do?

  • Get the basics down! Start here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-9804362/so-you-want-to-be-a-concept-reviewer
  • Read! The Guide Hub "critter resources" section: http://www.scp-wiki.net/guide-hub#toc4 has some resources you can use to practice different kinds of critique, as well as improving your reviewer skills overall.
  • Practice! There are always plenty of authors looking for feedback in the forums.

I'm interested in being a commander/mentor! How do I put my name forward for consideration?

Simply send a wikidot message to Zyn stating your interest, and noting which of the four criteria for giving greenlights you fulfill.

item.title: Want to earn Greenlighting Privileges and/or choose next month's front-page features?: Want to earn Greenlighting Privileges and/or choose next month's front-page features?
item.content:encoded:
Due to the ever-increasing demand for more skilled reviewers to help out in the forums, the Forum Criticism Staff Team has been holding 2-week mentoring sessions to train up-and-coming reviewers. These are called "Flights".1

What does being part of a Flight mean?

  • Flight 1 will run from February 1 to February 15. Flight 2 will run from February 15 to February 30.
  • Mentors (dubbed "commanders") will work with mentees ("officers") in the Writing Help forums to critique concepts and drafts while the officers practice and improve their critique skills.
  • At the start of the Flight, officers will determine their weekly goals for two categories: activity and quality. Activity can be something simple like "crit at least one thread a day", quality something like "be more familiar with matching authors to helpful resources/guides/example articles". Commanders will discuss these goals weekly.
  • Officers will be taught some forum management skills like how to respond (without backseat modding) to a thread that breaks guidelines.
  • If the officers cannot yet greenlight, they may officially recommend concepts to their commander for greenlight consideration.
  • Flight teams can have funny/rule of cool names. Commander discretion.

Who are the commanders this month?

The commanders for Flight 1 are Karablue9482 and TBA.

The commanders for Flight 2 are TBA.

Notice: for February, we are opening up commander signups to all individuals who currently have greenlighting privileges! If you're interested in learning about being a commander/mentor, please look at this page for more information.

Who can request consideration to be an officer?

Anyone! Newbies and veterans alike are welcome to put their names forth.

What do Flight participants get at the end?

  • For as long as the mentorship system continues, Flight teams will select the featured SCP, tale, and GoI format displayed on the front page of the site. Flight team member names will also be displayed on the front page of the site.2
  • Officers deemed ready by their commanders will be given greenlighting privileges (if they do not have them already), and their names and number of successful Flights will be displayed on the Butterfly Squad Roster.
  • Flight team member names will be displayed on the corresponding month's Site News page. Officers may optionally provide "flight signoff" messages where they briefly describe the experience and any parting words for future reviewer mentees.
  • (remember, provision of the rewards is up to commander discretion!)
Footnotes
1. Prepare for some Rule of Cool terminology, folks.
2. To accommodate six teams, the number of monthly front page features will be doubled.

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Second, I would call this Thaumiel instead of Safe. After all the Foundation’s using it to build cells for other SCPs.

I'm not entirely convinced this would be Thaumiel, since the entity itself isn't actively containing anything, it's just being a convenient builder. The Foundation could easily contain the same anomalies with structures built out of mundane items that fundamentally serve the same purpose.

It just hijacks resources (probably by impersonating personnel or hacking computers?) in order to have its cells created.

This would be a big red flag for me. Thaumiel anomalies by nature need to be trustworthy, and if this thing is "hijacking" resources via any sort of underhanded shenanigans, that makes it inherently untrustworthy and unreliable. Does the Foundation have any sort of control over its loyalty? Do they have any reassurance it won't spontaneously go rogue?

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity: Re: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Thank you, I agree it probably is Thaumiel, not Safe - good call. The draft I've already written is quite short.

As for its "powers" it somehow "sees" the future insofar as it creates cells to contain itself that are specifically tailored to some future SCP. It just hijacks resources (probably by impersonating personnel or hacking computers?) in order to have its cells created.

The references to other SCP's is just a quick call out to unique cells to "prove" that it somehow has precognition for what cells to construct.

item.title: New SCP idea in need of greenlighting: New SCP idea in need of greenlighting
item.content:encoded:
So I decided to try writing an SCP article. Btw, I already have a draft written on the SCP sandbox site but the idea needs to be greenlighted first, so here you go!

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout with the new ACS + incident reports, interview logs, recovery log, etc.

Elevator Pitch: Short pitch: It's a sentient toy troll that can move and talk that carries a mycotoxin that, when inhaled, makes the subject turn into a mindless zombie covered in hair. The mindless zombie covered in hair will attempt to hug any human close to it, which will spread the infection.

+ show block
– hide block

Longer pitch

This SCP is a Euclid class anomaly. It is a sentient toy resembling Fuzzbert, a character from the Trolls movie. It is capable of movement and speech, although its speech has to be translated using an unknown device. When it is disturbed or feels endangered it lets out a mycotoxin (SCP-XXXX-1) that, when inhaled by a human or any other living organism in the class Mammalia, attacks the brain causing growth hormone modifications, which results in accelerated hair growth starting from the subjects head and ending around its pelvic region. Hair growth can also be seen from the subject's eyes, nostrils, ears, mouth, and below the fingernails. After a certain amount of time, the subjects (now referred to as SCP-XXXX-2) cognitive functions will become limited and it will attempt to hug any human it comes in contact with, which will result in the infection spreading to that person. SCP-XXXX-2 instances mainly show interest in humans, but other living organisms in the class Mammalia that come in contact with it will develop the same symptoms.

Central Narrative: On January 8. 2009. a boy was playing near an old Russian nuclear power plant when he found a weird toy that started walking towards him making weird gurgling noises. The boy got very curious and decided to pick the toy up. The toy started shaking and let out a cloud of green mist. The boy got scared and ran home, taking the toy with him. After a few minutes, he started having flu-like symptoms, with tingling sensations around his nose. He started growing massive amounts of hair around his body and started attacking his own mother. Obviously scared, she called the police. The police arrived shortly after and found a creature covered in hair trying to break into a room. They neutralized the creature and contacted the SCP Foundation shortly after. When the Foundation arrived, they found a small toy that was walking around the house. They figured that that toy was the cause of the incident. They immediately sedated it and transported it to Site-██, where it currently resides. It was classified as a Euclid level SCP and given the number XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I feel like this SCP is a mix of multiple other existing SCPs but still has originality. It is interesting how mysterious its origin is, no one currently knows how it came to be or why it infects people, or how it can communicate with other people, or why instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are only interested in humans but can infect other animals as well. But those questions might be answered in the future… I also feel like the symptoms of the infection are pretty interesting, with all the hair growth and trying to hug people.

Additional Notes: So I already made a sandbox article, but I still think it needs some working to be done on it. Also, I was thinking of slowly answering all the questions about the SCP through interview logs and stuff, and also doing some SCP cross-links if you're ok with it. I will post the draft link here if you want.


Author, please note the Ideas Critique required reading wordcount limit; your post is about 160 words over. Please address this before seeking further feedback. ~Zyn

item.title: New SCP Idea: New SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, an addendum or two, and 2 ethics committee reports

Elevator Pitch: A man with severely burned skin who claims to have gone to the Christian hell. His skin will anomalously smolder and catch on fire at random intervals.

Central Narrative: One day, a man drenched in fire ran out of a burning building. It took a while to put him out and calm him down, but it was a mystery as to how he survived. The Foundation was alerted when his burns refused to heal and even got hotter, sometimes causing fires.

The man claimed to be Junior Toure, an Angolan man who died 67 years before he was found by The Foundation. His skin stayed burned and caught on fire randomly, but that was easily dealt with in the form of automatic sprinklers.

The man claimed to have gone to what he believed to be the Christian interpretation of hell, claiming to have seen glimpses of an endless field with people laying on the ground, bound by chains, forever on fire, the flames growing ever hotter.

He was in constant pain. He cried regularly and screams could be heard from his cell for hours on end. There was no way to help him. Eventually, a grievance with the ethics committee was filed, asking them if he should be put out of his misery. After an interview, he said "I don't want that. I don't want to return."

+ show block
– hide block

Toure aged normally, and as he did, his mental state deteriorated. He became paranoid and erratic, fearing death and a return to that hellish place. He died insane, with the only resemblance of peace being him requesting that his body be put in the ocean, saying "It might dull the pain while I'm down there."

His body burned nonstop after he died, with nothing being able to stop it. It eventually turned into a pile of ash. Another ethics committee grievance was filed, asking for Toure's last wish to be granted. The committee stipulated that if the ash had no anomalous properties, then it was to be dispersed in the Pacific Ocean.

The ash was found to be non-anomalous, and the dead man's wish was fulfilled. His ashes found their way to the bottom of the ocean, bearing a stark contrast to what he was bound to for eternity to come.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a very dark SCP, which is nothing new, but it would also be a neutralized SCP.

Additional Notes:
